title: Opt-in close commit, docs, and release

tasks.title: Implement the path-isolated close-commit engine
tasks.description: Create src/cli/core/close-commit.ts exporting commitCloseArtifacts({ cwd, paths, scope, sprintN, title }) returning { status: 'committed'|'skipped'|'failed', sha?, reason?, manualCommand? }. Guards return skipped with a reason: not a repository/git unavailable, no commits, detached HEAD, merge/rebase/cherry-pick/revert in progress (rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD, REBASE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, REVERT_HEAD, rebase-merge, rebase-apply), any close path ignored by git (check-ignore), no close path with changes. Otherwise run git add -- <changed close paths> then git commit --only -F <message> -- <paths>, with message 'chore(kyro): close <scope> sprint <n> — <title>' and a trailer block 'Kyro-Scope: <scope>' / 'Kyro-Sprint: <n>'. Never push, amend, --no-verify, or --no-gpg-sign; honor hooks and signing config. Any git failure returns failed with a short stderr summary and the exact manual command; it never throws.
tasks.context: Finding 03; R8, R9, R10, R11. git commit --only preserves other index entries but rejects paths unknown to git, so close paths are added explicitly first. execFileSync with array args, no shell (pattern of git-capture.ts). Use git --no-optional-locks for status calls (rule git-readonly-status). Test repos isolate global config (empty hooksPath dir, gpgsign false) except where a hook is the subject.
acceptance_criteria: In a temp repo with an unrelated file pre-staged and another modified, the commit contains exactly the changed close paths, the unrelated staged file remains staged and uncommitted, and the other change remains unstaged — proven by npm run check:sprint-close-commit.
The commit message matches the format and git interpret-trailers --parse returns Kyro-Scope and Kyro-Sprint; git log --grep 'Kyro-Sprint: <n>' finds it — proven by the same check.

Each guard (non-repo, unborn, detached, rebase in progress, ignored close path, nothing to commit) returns skipped with its reason and creates no commit; a pre-commit hook that exits 1 returns failed with a manual command and no commit; a passing hook still runs — proven by the same check.
npm run build and npm run check:git-trackability pass.

phases.title: Close wiring, parity, and compatibility
phases.objective: Run the commit only after a verified close on both surfaces, expose structured results, and warn mixed-version teams.

tasks.title: Wire the commit into CLI and MCP close with structured results
tasks.description: Implement one post-close step shared by executeConfirmedClose and the MCP closeSprintTool: after applySprintCloseTransaction and verifyWrittenSprint succeed, and only when resolveCommitOnSprintClose() is true, call commitCloseArtifacts with exactly the close write set (checkpoint, legacy snapshot, narrative, sprint.json, projectScopeWritePath()). Never run on --dry-run or unconfirmed MCP calls. CLI text prints the commit result; CLI --json data and the MCP applied result both carry { git, commit, warnings[] } with the dirty warning as structured text (debt-4). On a resumed close whose checkpoint has no close.git, report 'not recorded at the original close attempt' instead of a present-time reason (debt-5). Add outcome 'preview'/'applied' to plan sprint-mode --json data (debt-6). Add an MCP close assertion for git/commit/warnings.
tasks.context: Finding 04; R7, R12; debt-4, debt-5, debt-6. CLI close: close-sprint.ts executeConfirmedClose (~103); MCP: mcp/handlers.ts closeSprintTool (~91). The commit happens after the transaction, so it never affects checkpoint content (rule arch-frozen-close-inputs). The state-writer lock is outside the commit set by construction.
acceptance_criteria: With the preference true, a confirmed CLI close and a confirmed MCP close in equivalent temp repos each create one close commit and return the same commit shape plus git and warnings; with it absent or false no commit is created — proven by npm run check:sprint-close-commit.
close-sprint --dry-run and an MCP close without confirm create no commit even with the preference true — proven by the same check.

A close resumed from a checkpoint without close.git reports 'not recorded at the original close attempt', and plan sprint-mode --json data includes outcome — proven by npm run check:sprint-git-traceability.
